title: Integrity agreements with the federal inspector general
question: Which providers based in the Bay Area, or operating here under the same name, have signed a compliance agreement with the federal health inspector general?
finding: The inspector general's list holds 334 agreements, 43 with California parties. 3 are with parties based in the six Bay Area counties: Semler Scientific (Campbell, effective 2025); Braden Partners, LP Doing Business As Pacific Pulmonary Services (Novato, closed 2023); The County of San Mateo and San Mateo Medical Center (San Mateo, effective 2021). 4 more are with parties elsewhere whose name matches a Bay Area nursing-home chain, equipment supplier or hospice in the federal files. 3 of the 7 are in effect.
how: The inspector general's published list of corporate integrity agreements and similar agreements, as downloaded. A row is kept when the party's city is in one of the six Bay Area counties (city placed in a county with the federal relief-payment file's city table), or when the party's name matches the name of a nursing-home chain, nursing home, equipment supplier or hospice in the Bay Area files used on this page. Name matches compare the first legal name in the agreement with the provider name after dropping punctuation, and need at least two words.
limits: The list gives a party, a place, a kind of agreement and a status, and states no wrongdoing; why each agreement was signed is in the document behind the link. A name match is only a name match: a national company and a Bay Area branch may be different legal entities, and the agreement may concern conduct in another State. The list shows only agreements the inspector general currently publishes; older ones drop off. What each agreement covers is in the document behind the link.
